headline: Robots extend physical capability—letting computers act in the real world
universal_truth: The gap between knowing and doing is vast; thinking and acting require different capabilities
fun_facts: The word 'robot' comes from a Czech word meaning forced labor—coined in a 1920 play
Surgical robots can make movements smaller than a human hand could achieve
Most robots don't look humanoid—factory robots are just arms, warehouse robots are wheeled boxes
discussion_questions: What tasks are robots better at than humans?
What might robots never be able to do?
How do you feel about robots taking over certain jobs?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Computers can calculate, but they can't pick up a glass of water. Robots bridge that gap—giving computers bodies to act in the physical world. A robot is a computer that can do, not just think.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Robots can weld cars perfectly and assemble electronics precisely. But they struggle to fold laundry or walk on uneven ground. What's hard for robots that's easy for humans?
cliff.prompt: Why is physical interaction so hard for robots?

options.text: The real world is messy and unpredictable—it requires constant adaptation that rigid programming handles poorly
options.response: Yes. Your brain constantly adjusts to friction, weight, texture, and surprise. Robots excel at repetitive precision, not adaptive flexibility.

options.text: We haven't developed strong enough motors and sensors yet
options.response: Hardware matters, but the deeper challenge is handling unpredictable situations...

q1.title: Precision Strength
q1.script: Robots excel at tasks requiring tireless precision: welding, painting, assembling tiny electronics. They don't get tired, distracted, or inconsistent. For repetitive, precise work, robots are superhuman.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Precision Strength"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Dangerous Duty
q2.script: Robots go where humans shouldn't: nuclear reactors, deep ocean, burning buildings, bomb disposal. They can be lost without tragedy. Robots extend human reach into dangerous environments.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Surgical Precision
q3.script: Surgical robots don't operate alone—surgeons control them. But they provide superhuman precision: movements smaller than human hands can make, no tremor, perfect consistency. Human judgment plus robotic precision.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Thinking and acting require different capabilities. Robots teach that bridging mind and world is hard. We often underestimate physical skills because our bodies make them seem easy.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 118. Tomorrow, we'll explore how AI learns. Until then, appreciate what your body does effortlessly that even advanced robots struggle with.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Physical Intelligence - Appreciate Your Body
growTrack.learning_objective: Recognize the sophistication of physical capabilities
growTrack.activity: Do something 'simple' with your hands: pour water, tie a shoelace, catch a ball. Notice the constant adjustments you make without thinking. This physical intelligence took millions of years to evolve—and robots are just beginning to match it.
